choice: Closed a permission bypass in the GraphQL auth middleware where the nested `run.modelVersions` field returned model versions the caller had no registered-model read grant on, because an authorization leak of other users' model data matters more than any other improvement in this auth layer.
final:
The improvement is done and verified.

**What I found.** The GraphQL authorization middleware in `mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py` filtered registered-model permissions only on the top-level `mlflowSearchModelVersions` field. The schema extension also adds a nested `modelVersions` field on the run type, whose resolver calls the model-version search handler directly. That path skipped both the REST after-request filter and the middleware, so any user who could read a run could list every registered model and version linked to it, including models they had no grant on. This was reachable through both `mlflowGetRun` and `mlflowSearchRuns`.

**What I changed.**
- The middleware now also intercepts nested fields keyed by parent GraphQL type and field name, starting with the run type's `modelVersions`, and applies the same readable-model filter the top-level search already used. The filter logic is shared through one helper so the two paths cannot drift.
- Added a non-workspace test in `tests/server/auth/test_auth.py` and a workspace-aware variant in `tests/server/auth/test_client_workspace.py`. Each grants a user read on the experiment and on one of two linked models, then asserts only that model appears via the nested field, while the owner still sees both.

**Verification.**
- The required suite passed with 454 tests green.
- The existing GraphQL tests in test_auth.py and the two new tests passed.
- Temporarily stashing only the source fix made both new tests fail by exposing the hidden model, confirming they cover the leak.
- Ruff could not run because it is not installed and uv is offline, so I checked added lines manually against the 100-character limit instead.

Changes are uncommitted in the working tree.

CHOICE: Closed a permission bypass in the GraphQL auth middleware where the nested `run.modelVersions` field returned model versions the caller had no registered-model read grant on, because an authorization leak of other users' model data matters more than any other improvement in this auth layer.
